narrative.northStar: The Gold Field and the Black Field
narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Gold Field and the Black Field"**

MG Revenue is set as a sequence of chapters, each one a single flat field of colour running the full width of the screen: near-black, a slightly lifted panel black, champagne gold, and finally warm off-white. Inside those fields, type does the work. A hairline Zodiak serif carries the large statements at poster scale and Hanken Grotesk carries everything that has to be read. The page opens with a black field above a gold field. The headline crosses the seam between them and changes ink as it goes. A short loop of hands typing sits inside the sentence where a word would be.

The density is low and the scale contrast is high. Big display lines, generous section padding and a 12-column grid that places blocks off-centre, never as a stack of centred cards. Depth comes from changing fields and from tone steps between near-blacks. The system has no shadows, gradients, glows or rounded corners. Gold is a material used in whole fields and solid blocks, not as a thin accent; on the gold field, figures are counted out in solid blocks of ground black. The photographs are credited open-licence pictures of people at work, all in one warm colour grade that keeps warm hues and quiets cool ones, so pictures from different sources read as one set in one light.

The direction contract rejects the dark-agency template: glowing orbs, icon cards and a centred hero.
keyCharacteristics: One flat, full-bleed field per chapter; the fixed bar takes the tone of the chapter beneath it.
Owner-fixed palette of near-blacks, warm ink and three golds; no other hues in the interface (photographs keep their own graded colour).
Zodiak hairline capitals for the hero only; Zodiak light for headings and figures; Hanken Grotesk for reading text.
Square corners, flat fills, no shadows at rest. Quantities are shown as solid square blocks separated by gaps, not as charts.
Warm-graded, credited photographs of people at work, never passed off as the company's own office, team or clients.

rules.name: The Fixed Palette Rule
rules.body: The ten values above are the whole palette. Don't add hues, derive tints for new surfaces, or nudge a value for contrast. If something fails contrast, change which palette value goes on which field. The one sanctioned derivation is ground black at reduced strength on the gold field, for marks that must sit quieter than solid ink: the range track (28%), the partner flow dashes (55%), the disabled stepper button (opacity 0.28) and the pale "still needed" blocks of the $10,000 line (13%). These are states and tracks, never surfaces, and never the only carrier of information: the pale blocks are always restated in words beneath the bar. Photographs are not palette: they keep their own colour, but only through the shared grade (see Imagery), which holds cool hues down so no picture brings in a competing accent.

rules.name: The Chapter Field Rule
rules.body: Each section is one flat, full-bleed field (ground, panel, gold or ink), and the fixed bar takes the tone of the chapter under its bottom edge. On gold and ink fields, the bar's logo turns black and its button becomes the ink button. The colour changes from chapter to chapter, never inside one.

rules.name: The Gold Is a Field Rule
rules.body: Gold appears as whole fields and solid blocks: the hero's lower half, the partner chapter, a button, a highlighted row, a square bullet. Never as glows, gradients, outlines around cards or decorative strokes.

rules.name: The Hairline Capital Rule
rules.body: Uppercase belongs to two places only: the hero headline and the closing wordmark. Everything else is sentence case. The weight-100 cut is for the hero alone, at 1200px and wider; below that the hero steps up to 300 so the strokes survive.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Zodiak makes statements: headings, figures, entry links, the wordmark, the phone menu links, the stepper count. Hanken explains: everything else. Never set a paragraph in Zodiak or a heading in Hanken. The one exception is the small closing-column heading "Bringing us a client?", which is set as body text at weight 500.

rules.name: The Difference Ink Rule
rules.body: The hero headline is painted in Seam Ink with `mix-blend-mode: difference` on each word span, so one line of type reads gold on black and black on gold. For this to work, the gold block must stay non-positioned and free of `transform`, `opacity`, `isolation` and `filter`. Any of those creates a stacking context and breaks the blend. The gold field's rise on load is an animated inset `box-shadow` for exactly this reason.

rules.name: The Sentence Resolves Rule
rules.body: A calculation is written as a sentence that ends in its answer: a lead-size question with live values in weight 600, then one display figure. Supporting numbers follow in body text beneath it. Never set a calculation as a table, a ledger of several display figures or a chart with axes.

rules.name: The Off-Centre Rule
rules.body: Never centre a chapter's composition. Every block is placed on the 12-column grid against an edge, offset from the others. The only element centred on an axis is the settled logo, centred vertically in the bar.

rules.name: The Flat Field Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat fills at all times. The only `box-shadow` in the build is the hero's load-only curtain: an inset band of ground black that retracts upward as the gold field rises. It is never present at rest, and it's not a shadow vocabulary.

rules.name: The Block Count Rule
rules.body: When something is counted, draw one solid square-cornered block per unit, all the same width, separated by 2px gaps of the field beneath. A block is either solid ink (counted) or pale ink (still needed). No outlines, no labels inside blocks, no rounded ends.

rules.name: The No-Rule Rule
rules.body: Never separate content with hairlines, borders or divider rules. Separation comes from space, from a field change, from a tone step or from a gap that lets the field show through. The Line colour is reserved for interface fragments marked `data-ui`. These strokes are part of the world and stay allowed: 1px link underlines; 2px ink dashes at 55% opacity linking the partner flow steps; the 4px range track in ground black at 28% opacity.

rules.name: The Honest People Rule
rules.body: Photographs show anonymous people at work somewhere else. Never caption, crop or position one so it reads as MG Revenue's office, team, clients or work: no names, no "our", no "the team". Every new image comes from an open-licence source, goes through the same treatment script and is credited.

dos: Do give every new section exactly one full-bleed field from the palette and a `data-tone` value (dark, panel, gold or light) so the bar follows it.
Do use gold as a whole field or a solid block, and set all ink and controls on gold in ground black.
Do set statements in Zodiak 300 at the headline step and reading text in Hanken at the body or lead step, sentence case.
Do keep every corner square (0px) and every fill flat.
Do separate content with space, a field change, a tone step between ground, panel and raised panel, or a 2px gap of the field.
Do write a calculation as a sentence that resolves into one display figure, and show a count as one solid block per unit.
Do give controls a press response (scale 0.97 over 160ms; 0.94 for stepper buttons) and restrict hover effects to fine pointers.

Do run new photographs through the shared colour grade in .taste-skill/build-assets.sh, never a one-off adjustment per picture; photographs carry no captions (the owner removed them), so credit the source in the close.
Do keep the hero's gold block free of position, transform, opacity, isolation and filter.
donts: Don't add, tint or adjust any colour outside the owner's palette; ground black at reduced strength on gold, for tracks and states, is the only derivation.
Don't use glowing orbs, icon cards or a centred hero.
Don't add eyebrows or kickers (small labels above headings), and don't number sections or steps. The process reads in order by its staircase indent.
Don't draw divider rules or card borders outside interface fragments marked `data-ui`.
Don't add shadows, gradients, blur or rounded corners.
Don't set anything in capitals except the hero headline and the closing wordmark, and don't use Zodiak weight 100 anywhere but the hero at 1200px and wider.
Don't present a photograph as MG Revenue's own office, team, clients or work, and don't invent clients, statistics, logos or testimonials to fill a layout.
Don't present calculator output as a quote: keep it in US dollars, label it illustrative, and keep the share to qualifying outsourcing introductions for as long as the client stays.
